sentenceSets.sentence: Her dispassionate analysis of the situation helped the group resist the panic that had overtaken it the previous day.

answerChoices.reasoning: Detachment implies standing apart from the group's predicament, but she is working to steady the very people around her, which means she is engaged while refusing to be swept up.
Objectivity concerns freedom from personal slant in the evidence, whereas what the group needed was an account untouched by the fear that had seized them the day before.
Impartiality is about not favoring a side, yet no sides are in dispute here; the danger the analysis counteracts is panic rather than partiality.
'Clinical' carries a chill that would have alienated a frightened group, while her analysis is what brought them back from panic.
Caution would counsel hesitation, but a panicking group is already frozen and needed something else from her.
Thoroughness concerns how much ground the analysis covered, which would not by itself explain why it calmed people who had been frightened.
Rationality describes sound reasoning in general, while the contrast the sentence draws is specifically with the feeling that had overtaken the group.
Sobriety suggests seriousness of manner, which panicking people also exhibit, so it does not mark what made her analysis different.
A frantic analysis would feed the panic rather than help the group resist it.
Impassioned argument is the opposite of what steadied a group already gripped by feeling.
Hysteria is the condition the group was recovering from, not the remedy she supplied.

sentenceSets.sentence: The coroner's report was deliberately dispassionate, listing injuries in the same flat register whether the victim was a stranger or a child.

answerChoices.reasoning: Neutrality concerns taking no side in a dispute, but the report has no adversaries to balance; what it withholds is any note of feeling about who the dead were.
A matter-of-fact manner is simply plain and unfussy, whereas the striking thing here is the suppression of the emotion a child's death would ordinarily draw out.
'Unsentimental' rules out only mawkishness, yet the flat register also excludes horror, pity, and indignation, none of which are sentimental.
Impersonality describes the absence of the writer's individual voice, while the sentence emphasizes the absence of feeling about the subject regardless of who the subject is.
Concision concerns length, and a long report could still keep the same flat register across every case.
Formality is a matter of register and convention that a report full of outrage could still observe.
Exhaustiveness concerns completeness of the list of injuries rather than the uniform tone in which they are recorded.
'Bureaucratic' implies procedural clutter and evasion, but the sentence presents the tone as a deliberate professional discipline.
A lurid report would dwell on horror, contradicting the flat register described.
Anguish is exactly the feeling the report withholds when the victim is a child.
Sentimentality would break the uniform tone the sentence says was maintained.

sentenceSets.sentence: Friends found him unnervingly dispassionate about the divorce, as though he were recounting a stranger's misfortune.

answerChoices.reasoning: A stoic is understood to feel the blow and endure it silently, but the comparison to recounting a stranger's misfortune suggests no private struggle is visible at all.
Indifference asserts that he genuinely does not care, whereas the friends observe only a manner, and it is the manner that unnerves them.
Composure implies holding steady under strain, which would reassure friends rather than unnerve them.
Being unmoved describes the absence of a reaction at one moment, while the friends are struck by the settled tone in which he speaks of his own life.
Reserve means saying little, but he is talking freely about the divorce; it is the way he talks that disturbs them.
Politeness is unremarkable among friends and would not prompt the word 'unnervingly.'
Vagueness would mean withholding details, yet the comparison to recounting a misfortune implies he gives a full account.
Distraction would show his mind elsewhere, but he is attending to the subject closely enough to narrate it.
Being distraught is the ordinary reaction his friends expected and did not find.
Bitterness is a strong feeling openly shown, at odds with the stranger's-misfortune comparison.
Tears would be the opposite of the flat delivery that unsettles his friends.
